reason: The membrane holds the first specimen, and placing it in the flight locker directly advances the goal of bringing it home.
expectation: I expect the membrane specimen to be secured in the flight locker, though there may be another step before it is ready for the journey.

alternatives.reason: Harvesting lettuce seems like the natural way to take some of the garden along, but I want to secure the specimen first.

effect: Placing the membrane in the flight locker completed the specimen goal, so the garden is the remaining task.
reaction: It was reassuring to see the first specimen secured for the journey.
reason: Harvesting the lettuce is the only offered combination and seems like the way to take some of the garden along.
expectation: I expect to harvest leaves that can be brought to the flight galley.

effect: The harvest produced departure lettuce leaves, ready to take to the flight galley.
reaction: It is a nice connection to the garden kept alive through the storm.
reason: The flight galley is the only offered combination and seems the natural place to prepare the leaves for the journey.
expectation: I expect the leaves to be prepared or stored for the flight, completing the garden goal.

effect: The leaves became a packed meal, completing the garden goal and the chapter.
reaction: The handful of green is a satisfying reminder of the garden's survival through the storm.

mostWorthwhile.text: Packing the lettuce for the flight gave the garden a tangible place in the departure.

leastWorthwhile.text: Harvesting the leaves was straightforward and offered little discovery on its own.

surprise.text: I expected the specimen might need another securing step, but placing it in the locker completed its goal.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the locker, harvest, and galley all had clear connections to the goals.

continue.text: I would be curious to see what the lab learns from the specimens, though this chapter's actions themselves offered few decisions.
